title: FIR Filed After Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi Sit-In at Akashvani Bhawan
excerpt: Delhi Police booked the Gandhi siblings and INDIA bloc MPs for forcibly entering the premises during Tuesday's march against the Election Commission, after an eight-hour dharna that saw around 260 protesters detained.
body:
• Delhi Police registered an FIR on Wednesday against Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other INDIA bloc MPs for allegedly forcibly entering the Akashvani Bhawan premises on Tuesday.
  • The sit-in followed an eight-hour dharna inside the premises after police stopped an opposition march toward the Election Commission headquarters; around 260 people, including 10 MPs, were detained and later released.
  • The protest centered on the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and alleged irregularities under CEC Gyanesh Kumar, with the opposition raising the issue of "vote chori" and demanding his resignation.
  • NDTV reported the unannounced sit-in caught some INDIA bloc partners off guard, adding strain to the alliance even as it projects unity against the poll panel.

The Delhi Police has registered an FIR against Congress MPs Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, and the INDIA bloc leaders who accompanied them, for allegedly entering the Akashvani Bhawan premises without permission during Tuesday's opposition march against the Election Commission. The FIR was filed on Wednesday morning after a complaint was received about the forced entry, officials said.

The Gandhi siblings were among the protesters who gathered inside the Akashvani Bhawan compound after being stopped from marching toward the Election Commission's headquarters, Nirvachan Sadan, which sits about 300 metres away. They sat under a tree on the premises for more than eight hours before being detained and released later that night.

An eight-hour standoff in the heart of Delhi

Tuesday's march began at Parliament House, with INDIA bloc MPs heading toward Nirvachan Sadan. The Delhi Police said no application seeking permission for the march had been submitted to the Deputy Commissioner of Police, New Delhi, and no permission was granted. Protesters were stopped on Parliament Street near Akashvani Bhawan and the NITI Aayog office, where several layers of police barricades had been set up.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2107800801246920816

After being prevented from proceeding, the leaders sat on the road and continued their protest. Rahul Gandhi climbed onto one of the barricades and waved a large national flag, drawing loud slogans of support from the INDIA bloc leaders and workers gathered there. Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee was also seen climbing over a barricade. Holding tricolours and banners reading "Save democracy," the MPs raised slogans against the CEC, the BJP and the RSS.

The leaders then pushed through the reception gate of Akashvani Bhawan and entered the premises despite being stopped by police, according to IANS. Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi and Congress MP Deepender Hooda were seen sitting under a tree inside. Others present included Congress General Secretary K.C. Venugopal, Pawan Khera, Imran Pratapgarhi and Amarinder Singh Raja Warring. Police warned the demonstration could not continue through the night, but the protesters refused to leave until a delegation of MPs was allowed to meet Election Commission officials.

Officers eventually moved in, removed the protesters and detained them. Around 260 people, including 10 MPs, were detained, according to police, and taken to the New Police Lines in Kingsway Camp before being released hours later.

The spark: electoral rolls and "vote chori"

The demonstration was centered on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, with opposition parties demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and alleging irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission. The protest is part of the opposition's broader "Save Democracy" campaign against the poll panel.

Pawan Khera told reporters the optics made the case for them. "The Election Commission is right next to us, and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha is not being allowed to go to the Election Commission; he has been stopped," he said. "The Election Commission is barely 100 metres from here, and when the Leader of Opposition wants to go there and submit a memorandum, he is being stopped, and everyone is being stopped very harshly. This is the state of democracy in the national capital of this country."

"To save the traitors of democracy, the remnants of democracy have been dragged through the mud. There will be a reckoning — not a single traitor will be spared."

— Rahul Gandhi, in a post on X after his detention

What the FIR changes

Wednesday's FIR escalates a political protest into a legal case. Police said the case relates to the alleged unauthorised entry into Akashvani Bhawan and the subsequent sit-in; the specific sections invoked were still awaited. Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge questioned Union Home Minister Amit Shah over the detention of opposition leaders.

The filing also lands amid visible friction within the opposition alliance itself. NDTV reported that the surprise sit-in caught some INDIA bloc partners off guard, and the march included support from the BJD — an outside ally rather than a bloc member — underlining that the opposition's coalition arithmetic remains delicate even when the parties share a target.

The diaspora angle

Election-integrity battles are among the most closely followed Indian political stories among the diaspora, where debates over the credibility of the world's largest electoral exercise travel fast on social media. The Akashvani Bhawan sit-in, and Rahul Gandhi's barricade-top flag-waving, is the kind of imagery likely to dominate NRI political conversation for days.

What's next

The FIR's contours — the sections invoked, the named accused — will determine whether this becomes a short-lived political skirmish or a longer legal battle. The opposition's SIR and "vote chori" campaign shows no sign of winding down, and the poll panel's response to the memorandum the MPs tried to deliver will set the tone for the next round.
